headline: CMR Green Technologies publishes financial results for Q2 and H1 ending September 30, 2026
hook: Half-year numbers out at CMR Green
summary: CMR Green Technologies has formally notified the exchange about the release of its financial results for the second quarter and the first half of the financial year ending September 30, 2026. The press release details the company's financial performance during this period. Such corporate filings are part of mandatory disclosures for listed entities to keep shareholders and regulators informed. Retail investors tracking the company can review these disclosures to assess its recent financial health and operational progress.
whats_next: Detailed financial statement analysis by market participants
why_it_matters: Quarterly metrics guide near-term stock performance for shareholders.

headline: CMR Green Technologies Q2 net profit jumps 30% to Rs 66 crore
hook: Profit rises despite shrinking margins at CMR
summary: CMR Green Technologies reported a 30 percent increase in net profit to 66 crore rupees for the second quarter, alongside a 59 percent rise in revenue. The financial performance was achieved despite a contraction in profit margins during the period. The company operates in the metal recycling and green technology sector. Retail investors should note the company's revenue growth trajectory and margin pressures.
why_it_matters: Higher revenue offsets margin contraction for CMR Green.

summary: CMR Green Technologies Limited has formally notified the stock exchange about the acquisition of a new corporate office premises. This is a routine corporate real estate transaction with no immediate financial impact on the company's earnings. Indian retail investors tracking small-cap stocks can treat this as procedural operational news.

hook: New CFO takes charge at CMR Green

headline: CMR Green Technologies submits dematerialisation compliance certificate to SEBI
hook: Routine regulatory filing for CMR Green
summary: CMR Green Technologies has filed its dematerialisation compliance certificate with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI). This is a standard regulatory requirement for companies to ensure their shares are held in electronic form. The filing confirms the company's adherence to depository regulations. It does not impact the company's financial performance or stock valuation.
